title: Per-IP rate limiting for the public search endpoint

completion_criteria.text: A burst above the limit from one address is rejected with 429 and a Retry-After header naming whole seconds.
completion_criteria.result: npm test -- test/ratelimit/burst.test.ts exit 0, 7 pass 0 fail. Retry-After asserted as whole seconds against a skewed client clock.

completion_criteria.text: Two distinct addresses never share a budget.
A restart never lets a currently-blocked address through early.
The limit and the window are configuration validated at startup, never constants.
completion_criteria.result: npm test -- test/config/ratelimit-config.test.ts exit 0, 11 pass 0 fail. Startup refuses a non-integer and any value below 1, and the refusal names the variable.

artifacts.label: the spec, invariants I1-I4 and rulings H1-H2

spine.active_goal: The public search endpoint holds one budget per address that survives a restart and does not multiply behind more than one instance. Config and the 429 path are done; the Redis bucket is written but racy, and restart safety is blocked behind it.

open_risks.text: The token bucket read-modify-write is three Redis round trips, so two simultaneous requests from one address can both observe the last token and both consume it. The limit is exceeded under concurrency and the burst test does not catch it because it fires sequentially.
Retry-After may need to be an HTTP-date rather than seconds for CDN compatibility, which would contradict ruling H2.

key_decisions.title: The budget lives in Redis as a token bucket, not in process memory
